newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan withdraws arrest order on Bhutto husband.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan withdraws arrest order on Bhutto husband.

text.p: Pakistani authorities have withdrawn an order under which ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto's husband Asif Ali Zardari has been detained for three weeks, a court was told on Wednesday.

But it was not immediately known whether Zardari, arrested on November 5 when President Farooq Leghari dismissed Bhutto's government on charges of corruption and misrule which she denies, had been released or re-arrested under a fresh order.

No charges have been brought against Zardari, who was investment minister in Bhutto's cabinet, and the former prime minister had challenged his detention before the Punjab province's Lahore High Court.

The provincial government's advocate-general, Zafar Pasha, told the court on Wednesday the detention order issued against Zardari in Rawalpindi under a Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance had been withdrawn, court officials said.
The court then cancelled the petition, they said.
Soldiers seized Zardari at the governor's house in Lahore, where he had been staying, in the early hours of November 5, shortly after Leghari abruptly ended Bhutto's three-year rule.

The caretaker government led by Prime Minister Meraj Khalid first said Zardari, kept incommunicado for 48 hours, was being held in protective custody. Later it cited the Maintenance of Public Order ordinance to justify his detention.
On Tuesday, Bhutto and her three children met Zardari at a resthouse near Islamabad where he has been detained.
In 1994, Zardari was cleared of the last of 13 similar charges brought against him after the first Bhutto government was dismissed by presidential order four years earlier.
